name: Jumping Jack
summary: A foundational calisthenic exercise where you repeatedly jump to a wide stance while raising the arms overhead, then return together.

setup: Stand tall with feet together and arms resting naturally at your sides.
Keep your chest upright, core engaged, and gaze straight ahead.
steps: Jump lightly off the balls of your feet, spreading your legs out wider than shoulder-width.
Simultaneously sweep your arms out to the sides and overhead until your hands meet or nearly touch above your head.
Without pausing, spring off the balls of your feet to bring your legs back together while lowering your arms back to your sides.
Land softly with knees slightly bent and immediately rebound into the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Maintain a steady, rhythmic breathing pattern, inhaling as your limbs spread and exhaling as they return.

common_faults.fault: Landing flat-footed with locked knees, transmitting high impact to joints.
common_faults.correction: Land softly on the balls of your feet and maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout.

common_faults.fault: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) during the wide landing.
common_faults.correction: Track your knees outward in line with your toes as you land in the wide stance.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the arm motion short by only raising to shoulder height.
common_faults.correction: Sweep arms through a full range of motion until hands nearly touch overhead.

precautions: Perform on a flat, non-slip surface with supportive athletic footwear.
